summary: The selinux-policy group is the Android SELinux policy set carried in this image: 51 files across system_a (22), system_ext_a (15), vendor_a (11) and odm_a (3). It holds the platform policy source in CIL (plat_sepolicy.cil, 28,911 lines, mls true, 27 sids, 4 policycaps), vendor and system_ext policy sources (vendor_sepolicy.cil, system_ext_sepolicy.cil), a versioned platform public policy (plat_pub_versioned.cil, 2,077 names suffixed _32_0) that vendor policy builds on, one precompiled binary policy on odm (header reports SE Linux policy v30), per-version mapping files (26.0 to 32.0) with compat stubs, label and lookup tables (file_contexts, seapp_contexts, property_contexts, service_contexts, hwservice_contexts, keystore2_key_contexts), signature-to-seinfo XML tables, a denial-metadata table, and a platform version file reading 32.0. Two checksum records per partition bind the precompiled policy to its inputs; the platform and system_ext records were recomputed and match the concatenation of policy source plus mapping/32.0.cil. Init and libselinux reference these paths by name. Commands in the evidence use M=<image>/mnt (mounted, read-only) and W=<image>-tools/work/subsystems/selinux-policy.

claims.label: verified
claims.claim: plat_sepolicy.cil is 28,911 lines and 1,897,754 bytes of CIL. It opens with role, handleunknown deny, mls true, four policycaps (network_peer_controls, open_perms, extended_socket_class, nnp_nosuid_transition), 27 sids and their sidcontext forms, and a MLS range of c0 to c1023.
claims.evidence: wc -l <image>/mnt/system_a/system/etc/selinux/plat_sepolicy.cil -> '28911'. head -n 30 plat_sepolicy.cil excerpt: '(handleunknown deny)', '(mls true)', '(policycap network_peer_controls)', '(policycap open_perms)', '(policycap extended_socket_class)', '(policycap nnp_nosuid_transition)', '(sid devnull)', '(sidcontext devnull (u object_r null_device ((s0) (s0))))'. grep -E '^\(userrange ' plat_sepolicy.cil -> '(userrange u ((s0 ) (s0 (range c0 c1023))))'. grep -c '^(sid ' -> 27.
claims.reason: wc -l gives 28911 and stat gives 1897754 bytes. sid count 27 and sidcontext count 27 match. policycap lines 8-11 match. The userrange line is (userrange u ((s0 ) (s0 (range c0 c1023)))): the low level is s0 with no categories, and the high level is s0 with the category range c0 through c1023. c0 and c1023 are category bounds, not a sensitivity range, so 'MLS range of c0 to c1023' is misleading. The opening also has three role declarations and two cil_gen_require lines (lines 4-5) before handleunknown (line 6) and mls (line 7).
claims.corrected_claim: plat_sepolicy.cil is 28,911 lines and 1,897,754 bytes of CIL. It opens with three role declarations and two cil_gen_require lines, then (handleunknown deny) and (mls true), four policycaps, and 27 sids with their sidcontext forms. The user u range runs from s0 with no categories to s0 with the category range c0 through c1023.

claims.claim: vendor_sepolicy.cil is 388,964 bytes and 1,190 lines of CIL forms, with 2,150 allow, 436 type, 200 genfscon, 146 dontaudit, 130 typetransition, 86 neverallow and 25 allowx forms. It defines procfs genfscon labels for /sys/kernel and /debugdriver paths and typetransitions into _32_0 domains.

claims.reason: wc -l gives 3951 lines (grep -c '' also 3951; 3950 top-level forms). The claimed 1,190 lines does not hold. Byte size 388964, allow 2150, type 436, genfscon 200, dontaudit 146, typetransition 130, neverallow 86 and allowx 25 all match. typetransition: 130 rules. The source is a _32_0 domain in 122 (for example init_32_0), but the resulting default type carries no suffix in all 130 (for example hal_atrace_default). The claim 'typetransitions into _32_0 domains' is wrong. genfscon: 17 proc and 183 sysfs. Procfs rules include /sys/kernel (8) and /debugdriver/driverdump (1), plus other paths, so the procfs description is partial.
claims.corrected_claim: vendor_sepolicy.cil is 388,964 bytes and 3,951 lines (3,950 top-level forms): 2,150 allow, 436 type, 436 roletype, 277 typeattributeset, 200 genfscon (17 procfs, 183 sysfs), 146 dontaudit, 130 typetransition, 86 neverallow, 63 typeattribute and 25 allowx. Its 130 typetransition rules take a _32_0 source domain in 122 cases (for example init_32_0) and name an unsuffixed default type (for example hal_atrace_default).

gaps: The precompiled binary was parsed only as far as its 64-byte header. Its symbol tables, class and permission lists, avtab and ocontext records were not decoded, so the rule content of the binary is not known.
No policy was compiled or validated. secilc (system_a/system/bin/secilc, aarch64 ELF) was not executed, so the build flags, the target policy version and the compile output were not reproduced.

Init and libselinux reference paths that are not in the mounted partitions: /odm/etc/selinux/odm_sepolicy.cil and odm_*_contexts, /product/etc/selinux/product_sepolicy.cil and product_*_contexts, /vendor/etc/selinux/nonplat_sepolicy.cil and nonplat_*_contexts, /vendor/etc/selinux/precompiled_sepolicy, /debug_ramdisk/userdebug_plat_sepolicy.cil and /mfgmode_plat_sepolicy.cil. Their contents and existence were not checked.
The label hal_drm_service (two entries in vendor_service_contexts) is declared in no mounted CIL file. The partition that declares it was not in the mount.

The file_contexts regexes at lines 642 and 644 name checksum files differently from the files on disk. The on-disk checksum files are labeled by the broader rules at lines 88 and 28. The intent behind the naming was not established.
Regex precedence in file_contexts (which of several matching entries the consumer applies) was not determined. Only the sets of matching entries were listed.
The certificates in the mac_permissions signature attributes were not decoded (subject, issuer, validity). Only the hex prefix was confirmed.
The embedded identifiers in the precompiled binary (for example vendor_service_contexts_file) were read from strings only. Their role in the binary is inferred.
The init binary is stripped. The path references come from strings, with no disassembly, so the order and conditions under which init loads each file were not established.
The contents of the compat stubs for 26.0, 28.0 and 29.0 (system_a) were not read. Their roles are inferred from file names and sizes.
The source of the version mismatch between the binary (v30) and the platform version (32.0) was not determined.
The bug references in selinux_denial_metadata (b/NNNNNNNN) were not resolved against any external source.
Declared-type counts (2,275) come from grepping '(type NAME' forms in five CIL files. They are not the output of a policy compile and do not include typealias or generated names.
Only the 51 group rows were examined. Other rows of classified.tsv that reference SELinux paths were not in this group and were not evaluated.
